beats: title: The story of this class: three families in the colonies of Texas, from the fall of 1835 to the spring of 1836.
arrival: Three families came to new land in the colonies, near Columbia, Gonzales and San Felipe de Austin.
call: Riders brought word that soldiers had come for the cannon at Gonzales. From one family men rode to join the volunteers. Two families kept to their farms.
fight: The fight at Concepción: Jasper Harrowgate.

fight: The Alamo: Cayetano Flashwright, Feliciano Flashwright and Jasper Harrowgate, from two families. Cayetano Flashwright was killed there. Feliciano Flashwright was killed there. Jasper Harrowgate was killed there.
news: Word that the Alamo had fallen reached the Harrowgate family on March 13, and the Flashwright family only on March 16, three days later.
flight: In March word came that the Mexican army was coming, and every family was told to leave for the east. Three families loaded their wagons and set out.
sickness: Sickness came to two families on the road and in the camps.
burned: Mexican foragers burned the farms of Anselmo's family and the Flashwright family. None of them knew it for days.
news: Word that Houston's army had won at San Jacinto reached the Harrowgate family on April 22, and Anselmo's family only on April 23, one day later.
home: After San Jacinto the families went home: one family to a house still standing, and two families to ashes. Three of the class's people did not come home from the war.
closing: Five of the class's people went to the war. Every family has its own story, and each of you will now see yours, on your own screen.

hh-1: home: The family came home. The house was ashes, burned by Mexican foragers. They found one cow and 5 hogs again.
rebuild: In the days after, they raked out the ashes and began again: the first logs of a new house went up where the old one had stood.
burial: The family gathered under the trees by the house to remember Feliciano and Cayetano, and set up two wooden markers in their memory.

count: Manuela sat down at the table to count what the family had left: 250 reales in coin, and one head of cattle and five hogs on the range. The farm was ashes: there was nothing left of it to sell.
hh-2: home: The family came home. The house was still standing. Jethro was already there, home since May 2.
burial: The family gathered under the trees by the house to remember Jasper, and set up a wooden marker in their memory.
count: Jethro sat down at the table to count what the family had left: 0 reales in coin.

sale: A land agent from Gonzales came out and bought the farm, the land, the round-log cabin, 30 acres of cleared field, fenced and the well, for 75 reales. With the coin in the house, the family had 75 reales.
